title: A Legal Winning Streak for Religion

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯 DealBook 的

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 在 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上，现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将对部分采访进行现场直播，任何人都可以于 nytimes.com 免费观看

sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日的直播。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，畅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: In a new ruling, the Supreme Court has given religious Americans their latest victory against government rules that the court says infringe on religious freedom.
sentences.zh: 在一项新的裁决中，最高法院让有宗教信仰的美国人在对抗政府规章的斗争中取得了最新胜利，法院称这些规章侵犯了宗教自由。

sentences.en: But as legal victories accumulate for the religious, the question has become whether the Supreme Court's majority is protecting the rights of the faithful
sentences.zh: 但随着宗教界法律胜利的累积，问题变成了最高法院的大多数派究竟是在保护信徒的权利

sentences.en: or giving them preference.
sentences.zh: 还是在给予他们特权。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Supreme Court reporter Adam Liptak.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事、最高法院记者亚当·利普塔克。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, April 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 4 月 14 日，星期三。

sentences.en: Adam, tell me about this Supreme Court ruling that was handed down a few days ago.
sentences.zh: 亚当，请跟我讲讲几天前下达的那项最高法院裁决。

sentences.en: So it's Friday night.
sentences.zh: 那是星期五晚上。

sentences.en: It's about 1130 at night.
sentences.zh: 大约是晚上 11 点 30 分。

sentences.en: I'm just about to go to bed and I get a call from the public information office at the court that the court has just handed down a ruling, which
sentences.zh: 我正准备睡觉，突然接到法院公共信息办公室的电话，说法院刚刚下达了一项裁决，

sentences.en: is, I'd like to say it's unusual, but it's happening more and more of these late night, Friday night rulings.
sentences.zh: 怎么说呢，我想说这很不寻常，但这种深夜尤其是周五晚上的裁决正变得越来越多。

sentences.en: And the court says that by a five to four vote, it's lifted restrictions imposed by California
sentences.zh: 法院以五比四的投票结果宣布，取消了加利福尼亚州

sentences.en: on religious services held in private homes.
sentences.zh: 对私人住宅内举行的宗教仪式的限制。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And explain that decision and the case that led to it.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下这项决定以及引发该案的诉讼背景。

sentences.en: Well, California has a bunch of COVID restrictions meant to thwart the spread of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 好的，加州有一堆旨在遏制大流行蔓延的新冠防疫限制措施。

sentences.en: One of them limits private gatherings in private homes to no more than three households.
sentences.zh: 其中一项将私人住宅内的私人聚会限制在最多三个家庭以内。

sentences.en: A couple of people who wanted to hold Bible study groups and prayer meetings in their private homes
sentences.zh: 有几个人希望在他们的私人住宅里举行圣经学习班和祈祷会，

sentences.en: for more than three households challenge this restriction, saying it violates their constitutional right to the free exercise of religion.
sentences.zh: 参与人数超过了三个家庭，他们对这一限制提出了挑战，称其违反了他们受宪法保护的宗教自由信奉权。

sentences.en: And when they say free exercise, what they mean is the constitutional protection in the First Amendment that prohibits the government from interfering with
sentences.zh: 当他们说自由信奉时，他们的意思是第一修正案中的宪法保护，该保护禁止政府干涉

sentences.en: the free exercise of religion with the ability of people to pursue their religious beliefs and practices.
sentences.zh: 宗教的自由信奉，即干涉人们追求其宗教信仰和实践的能力。

sentences.en: And the court agrees.
sentences.zh: 而法院表示赞同。

sentences.en: And what was the court's reasoning in letting those who want to gather for prayer in homes do so?
sentences.zh: 法院允许那些希望在住宅内聚会祈祷的人这样做的理由是什么？

sentences.en: The court's reasoning was essentially that these folks were being treated worse than other folks.
sentences.zh: 法院的理由本质上是这些人受到了比其他人更差的对待。

sentences.en: Now, it's true that on its face, this restriction applied to all kinds of private gatherings.
sentences.zh: 现在，诚然，从表面上看，这一限制适用于各种私人聚会。

sentences.en: Whether it's a Super Bowl party or a book group or a Bible study class, it applied to all private gatherings.
sentences.zh: 无论是超级碗派对、读书会还是圣经学习班，它都适用于所有私人聚会。

sentences.en: But the court says that's not the right way to ask the question.
sentences.zh: 但法院表示，这并不是提出问题的正确方式。

sentences.en: Is religion being treated worse than anything in any way comparable?
sentences.zh: 宗教受到的对待是否在任何方面都比任何可比事物更差？

sentences.en: And the court says we have to cast the net more broadly.
sentences.zh: 法院表示，我们必须撒一张更大的网。

sentences.en: And other things are comparable.
sentences.zh: 还有其他事物是具有可比性的。

sentences.en: You know, the supermarket is comparable.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，超市是可比的。

sentences.en: The tanning salon is comparable.
sentences.zh: 美黑沙龙是可比的。

sentences.en: The manicure shop is comparable.
sentences.zh: 美甲店是可比的。

sentences.en: The bowling alley is comparable.
sentences.zh: 保龄球馆是可比的。

sentences.en: And because there are no similar limits in those settings, the court says the free exercise rights of the folks who want to do religious
sentences.zh: 正因为这些场所没有受到类似的限制，法院表示，那些希望在自己家中进行宗教

sentences.en: gatherings in their homes had been violated.
sentences.zh: 聚会的人的宗教自由权受到了侵犯。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So in this ruling, a majority of the justices find that when it comes to a rule restricting everyone's ability to gather at home, the gathering
sentences.zh: 所以在这次裁决中，多数大法官认为，当涉及一项限制所有人居家聚会能力的规则时，那些希望聚在一起并在家中祈祷的

sentences.en: of religious people who want to get together and pray in their homes should be treated differently based on protections of religion in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 宗教人士的聚会，应当根据美国宪法中对宗教的保护受到不同的对待。

sentences.en: Constitution.
sentences.zh: 宪法。

sentences.en: So that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That captures what the majority said.
sentences.zh: 这准确概括了多数派的观点。

sentences.en: The dissent takes a different view.
sentences.zh: 持不同意见者则持截然不同的观点。

sentences.en: The dissent says, listen, this law applies equally to religion and non-religion.
sentences.zh: 异议意见指出，听着，这项法律对宗教和非宗教是一视同仁的。

sentences.en: The right way to think about it is, does it restrict religious people who want to gather in their homes more than non-religious people who want to gather in their homes?
sentences.zh: 正确的思考方式是：它是否比那些想要在家聚会的非宗教人士，更多地限制了想要在家聚会的宗教人士？

sentences.en: The answer to that is no.
sentences.zh: 答案是没有。

sentences.en: And the majority is hunting around and stretching matters to try to find things to compare these home gatherings to.
sentences.zh: 多数派四处搜寻并牵强附会，试图找出各种事物来与这些家庭聚会进行比较。

sentences.en: And it doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 这根本说不通。

sentences.en: So in dissent, Justice Elena Kagan says it's not the job of the court to compare apples to watermelons.
sentences.zh: 因此，埃ena·卡根大法官在反对意见中表示，法院的职责不是把苹果和西瓜进行比较。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: By which she meant you can't compare people gathering at home to pray with supermarkets.
sentences.zh: 她的意思是，你不能把聚在家里祈祷的人和超市相提并论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Adam, why does this ruling, which on its surface seems kind of small, right, home gatherings in a single one of our 50 states, why does it matter?
sentences.zh: 亚当，为什么这项从表面上看似乎很小的裁决——比如我们 50 个州中某一个州的家庭聚会——为什么它如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, it matters for at least two reasons, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，它之所以重要至少有两个原因。

sentences.en: One is it's an instance of an incredible winning streak for claims of religious liberty before this Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 其一是，这是最高法院审理的宗教自由诉求中取得惊人连胜纪录的一个事例。

sentences.en: So it's one of many.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是其中之一。

sentences.en: But it's one of many that has been undermining a principle the court announced in 1990 that neutral laws of general applicability apply to religion and everybody else.
sentences.zh: 但它是众多正在瓦解最高法院在 1990 年宣布的一项原则的案件之一，该原则即普遍适用的中立法律适用于宗教和所有人。

sentences.en: And I know that's a bit of jargon.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来有点专业术语。

sentences.en: But what it means is if there's a law that says everyone has to pay taxes, if you have a religious objection to paying taxes, tough luck.
sentences.zh: 但它的意思是，如果有一条法律规定每个人都必须纳税，如果你对纳税有宗教异议，那只能自认倒霉。

sentences.en: It's a neutral law of general applicability.
sentences.zh: 这是一条普遍适用的中立法律。

sentences.en: If there's a law that targets or singles out religion, sure, that deserves constitutional protection.
sentences.zh: 如果有一条法律专门针对或挑选出宗教，那当然应该受到宪法保护。

sentences.en: But a law that applies to everybody equally is constitutional.
sentences.zh: 但一项平等适用于所有人的法律是符合宪法的。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So where does that 1990 principle that laws should apply neutrally to all, including religious people, where exactly does that come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，1990 年确立的“法律应当对所有人（包括宗教人士）保持中立适用”这一原则究竟源自何处？

sentences.en: We'll hear argument next, number 88, 12, 13, employment division.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们将听取辩论，案号 88、12、13，就业署诉案。

sentences.en: It comes from a case called Employment Division versus Smith.
sentences.zh: 它源于一个名为“就业署诉史密斯案”的案件。

sentences.en: Does the free exercise clause require every state to exempt the religious payout of use by the Native
sentences.zh: 自由信奉条款是否要求每个州豁免印第安纳

sentences.en: American church?
sentences.zh: 美洲教会使用的宗教派息？

sentences.en: Or perhaps even beyond that.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至可能超出这个范围。

sentences.en: And the question in the case was whether Native
sentences.zh: 该案的核心问题是，作为宗教仪式的一部分而服用了派息的印第安纳

sentences.en: Americans who had taken payout as part of a religious ceremony were exempt from a law that barred illegal drug use.
sentences.zh: 美洲原住民是否可以豁免于一项禁止非法吸毒的法律。

sentences.en: They contend that a religious motivation for engaging in legally prohibited action places the
sentences.zh: 他们辩称，从事法律所禁止行为的宗教动机，使得

sentences.en: citizen beyond the reach of a law that is not specifically directed at his religious practice and that is conceitedly constitutional as applied to others.
sentences.zh: 公民超越了一项并非专门针对其宗教实践、且就适用于他人而言公认合宪的法律的管辖范围。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court in a decision by
sentences.zh: 最高法院在一项由

sentences.en: Justice Antonin Scalia, conservative justice, articulates the principle that we have been living with for many decades.
sentences.zh: 保守派大法官安东尼·斯卡利亚撰写的判决中，阐述了我们已经遵循了数十年的原则。

sentences.en: That an individual's religious beliefs do not exclude him from compliance with an otherwise valid law prohibiting conduct that the state is free to regulate.
sentences.zh: 即个人的宗教信仰并不能免除其遵守其他方面合法、禁止州有权监管行为的法律的义务。

sentences.en: So you don't get an exception just because you have a religious objection.
sentences.zh: 因此，你不能仅仅因为有宗教异议就能获得豁免。

sentences.en: To make an individual's obligation to obey such a law contingent upon the law's coincidence with his religious beliefs contradicts both constitutional tradition and common sense.
sentences.zh: 使个人服从此类法律的义务取决于该法律是否与他的宗教信仰相契合，这既违背了宪法传统，也违背了常识。

sentences.en: Now a law that actually targets religion, that disadvantages religion by design, completely different question.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果是一项真正针对宗教、在设计上使宗教处于不利地位的法律，则是完全不同的问题。

sentences.en: But laws that apply to everybody are constitutional even if they interfere with some aspect of religious practice.
sentences.zh: 但适用于所有人的法律是合宪的，即使它们干涉了宗教实践的某些方面。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: For example, a law like a COVID restriction in California saying no one can gather in their homes if there are more than three households.
sentences.zh: 例如，像加州新冠限制令那样，规定如果超过三个家庭，任何人不得在家中聚会的法律。

sentences.en: That would, under this principle, be considered neutrally applicable to everyone.
sentences.zh: 根据这一原则，这将被视为对所有人中立适用。

sentences.en: It would look like a classic example of that.
sentences.zh: 它看起来将是这方面的经典范例。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's guided the court until quite recently when there seems to be now a quite successful move to undermine it.
sentences.zh: 正是这一原则一直指导着法院，直到最近，现在似乎出现了一场相当成功的试图瓦解它的运动。

sentences.en: And when did that successful move to undermine it start to experience this success that you mentioned?
sentences.zh: 这种试图瓦解它的成功运动是从什么时候开始取得你所说的这种成功的？

sentences.en: So it's been accelerating and particularly since Chief Justice John Roberts joined the court in the court in 2005.
sentences.zh: 这一趋势一直在加速，特别是自从首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨于 2005 年加入法院以来。

sentences.en: But I'd say in the past couple years, the court has found a way to chip away at, undermine, hollow out the principle so that religious groups get special favoritism.
sentences.zh: 但我想说，在过去几年里，法院找到了一种方法来蚕食、瓦解、掏空这一原则，从而让宗教团体获得特殊的偏爱。

sentences.en: For example, in the last term, the term that ended in July, there were three major religion cases the religious group wins every time.
sentences.zh: 例如，在上一任期——即 7 月结束的任期内，有三个重大的宗教案件，宗教团体每次都赢了。

sentences.en: One question was, if states give tax benefits to private schools, do they have to give them also to religious schools?
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题是，如果各州向私立学校提供税收优惠，它们是否也必须向宗教学校提供？

sentences.en: I mean, this is a case about money and the question of whether or not it must go to religious schools.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个关于金钱以及资金是否必须流向宗教学校的问题。

sentences.en: Answer, yes.
sentences.zh: 答案是，是的。

sentences.en: Another question was, do religious schools, do Catholic schools have an exemption from employment discrimination laws?
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，宗教学校、天主教学校是否可以豁免于就业歧视法？

sentences.en: So you're asking for an exemption to the Family and
sentences.zh: 也就是说你要求豁免于《家庭与

sentences.en: Medical Leave Act to all sorts of laws?
sentences.zh: 医疗假法》以及各种各样的法律吗？

sentences.en: And the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 答案是，是的。

sentences.en: The religious group gets to set its own internal rules.
sentences.zh: 宗教团体可以制定自己的内部规则。

sentences.en: And finally, can religious employers opt out of the Obamacare contraception mandate requiring them to provide free contraception coverage to female workers?
sentences.zh: 最后，宗教雇主能否选择不遵守奥巴马医改中关于避孕药具的强制规定，即要求他们向女员工提供免费的避孕药具覆盖？

sentences.en: I'm talking about exempting a secular employee of a church from receiving the contraceptive coverage.
sentences.zh: 我说的是免除教会世俗员工获得避孕药具报销的义务。

sentences.en: The answer to that more or less was yes.
sentences.zh: 这个问题的答案多多少少也是肯定的。

sentences.en: So at the end of the last term, religious liberty is doing great.
sentences.zh: 所以在上一任期结束时，宗教自由发展得非常好。

sentences.en: It's on a winning streak with one exception.
sentences.zh: 它正处于连胜之中，只有一个例外。

sentences.en: In cases involving state restrictions on religious gatherings to combat the pandemic, the court has been sustaining those restrictions, saying that the government,
sentences.zh: 在涉及各州为抗击大流行而对宗教聚会进行限制的案件中，法院一直支持这些限制，称政府

sentences.en: even at the expense of impinging on religious liberty, has the right to protect public health.
sentences.zh: 即使以侵犯宗教自由为代价，也有权保护公众健康。

sentences.en: But that changes after Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg dies in September, is replaced by Justice Amy Coney Barrett,
sentences.zh: 但这种情况在 9 月露丝·巴德·金斯伯格大法官逝世、由艾米·科尼·巴雷特大法官接任后发生了变化，

sentences.en: and what had been 5-4 decisions in one direction, sustaining these restrictions, all of a sudden become 5-4
sentences.zh: 原本以五比四支持这些限制的判决，突然变成了以五比四

sentences.en: decisions in the opposite direction, where the religious groups start to win, where the court says they have a
sentences.zh: 走向相反方向的判决，宗教团体开始获胜，法院裁定他们拥有

sentences.en: constitutional right to gather in houses of worship and now in private homes, notwithstanding the public health interest on the other side.
sentences.zh: 在礼拜场所和现在的私人住宅内聚会的宪法权利，而不受对立的公共健康利益的影响。

sentences.en: So Adam, where does that winning streak end up leaving the Supreme Court on this question of religious liberty and this principle that laws should be neutrally applied?
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，这场连胜最终让最高法院在宗教自由这一问题以及“法律应当被中立适用”这一原则上处于什么位置？

sentences.en: The Supreme Court has figured out a way to undermine but not overthrow that principle.
sentences.zh: 最高法院已经找到了一种方法来削弱但并未推翻这一原则。

sentences.en: And the way it does it is to say, if any secular activity is treated better than religion, then religion must also be treated the same.
sentences.zh: 它采取的方法是宣称，如果任何世俗活动受到的待遇优于宗教，那么宗教也必须享受同等待遇。

sentences.en: And it's a very rare regulation that doesn't have an exception for something.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有哪项规章对某些事物是没有例外的。

sentences.en: And so long as you have an exception for something, the court is now saying religion also has to get that same exception.
sentences.zh: 只要你对某些事物有例外，法院现在就在说，宗教也必须获得同样的例外。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So if something is granted to anyone, it must also be granted to people of religion.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果某项权利赋予了任何人，也必须赋予宗教信徒。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the practical impact of that is to give claims of religious liberty special force and to give religious people and groups a kind of privileged status.
sentences.zh: 其实际影响是赋予了宗教自由诉求特殊的效力，并赋予宗教个人和团体一种特权地位。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is, by definition, not neutrality.
sentences.zh: 这按定义来说就不是中立。

sentences.en: It's preference.
sentences.zh: 而是偏袒。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And maybe that's right.
sentences.zh: 也许这本来就是对的。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, this 1990 rule may or may not be correct.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，1990 年的那条规则可能正确，也可能不正确。

sentences.en: But what we know for sure is that the new rule is different.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以确切知道的是，新规则与以往不同。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 完全解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Adam, why are these religious liberty cases so important to religious groups?
sentences.zh: 亚当，为什么这些宗教自由案件对宗教团体如此重要？

sentences.en: What is wrong with the world in which the law, as Justice Antonin Scalia articulated it, that the law does not apply as neutrally to the religious as it does to the non-religious?
sentences.zh: 按照大法官安东宁·斯卡利阿阐述的观点，为什么这个世界上的法律对宗教人士和非宗教人士不能一视同仁，这就是法律存在的问题吗？

sentences.en: And therefore, what's the legal and religious logic of bringing these cases to the Supreme Court?
sentences.zh: 因此，把这些案件闹到最高法院，其背后的法律与宗教逻辑是什么？

sentences.en: This is part of a societal split.
sentences.zh: 这是社会分裂的一部分。

sentences.en: Americans have become less religious over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，美国人变得越来越不虔诚。

sentences.en: Religious Americans have dug in and feel aggrieved that mainstream culture and developments in legislatures and at
sentences.zh: 有宗教信仰的美国人则固守立场，并感到委屈，因为主流文化、立法机构的发展以及

sentences.en: the Supreme Court, notably in the 2015 decision establishing a constitutional right to same-sex marriage, has left them out.
sentences.zh: 最高法院——尤其是2015年确立同性婚姻宪法权利的那项裁决——将他们抛在了身后。

sentences.en: And not only that, but kind of marginalized them and caricatured them as bigots when they're not on board for advances, as progressives would see it, in gay rights,
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们还被边缘化，在不支持同性恋权益方面——用进步派的话说——被刻画成冥顽不灵的狭隘之徒，

sentences.en: transgender rights, access to contraception, and so on.
sentences.zh: 跨性别者权益、获取避孕措施的途径等等。

sentences.en: So this is a legal fight, but also a culture wars fight.
sentences.zh: 所以这既是一场法律之争，也是一场文化战争之争。

sentences.en: The member of the court I associate most with the position that religion needs special protection these days is Justice Samuel Alito.
sentences.zh: 在法官中，我认为最符合“如今宗教需要特殊保护”这一立场的是塞缪尔·阿利托大法官。

sentences.en: I am very pleased to have this opportunity to speak to all of you who are attending the Federalist Society's annual lawyers convention via the internet.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能有这个机会，通过互联网向所有出席联邦党人协会年度律师大会的各位发言。

sentences.en: George W.
sentences.zh: 小布什

sentences.en: Bush appointee joins the court in 2006, both in his writings and his public comments, and notably
sentences.zh: 任命的法官于2006年加入最高法院，无论是在他的文章、公开言论中，还是特别

sentences.en: in a speech he gave back in November to the Federalist Society, the conservative legal group.
sentences.zh: 在他去年11月向保守派法律团体“联邦党人协会”发表的一场演讲中，都体现了这一点。

sentences.en: It pains me to say this, but in certain quarters, religious liberty is fast becoming a disfavored right.
sentences.zh: 我很痛心这么说，但在某些圈子里，宗教自由正迅速沦为一项不受欢迎的权利。

sentences.en: He really sketches out how the court needs to be doing more in this area because he says religious liberty is under assault.
sentences.zh: 他详细勾勒了法院需要在这一领域做更多工作的原因，因为他称宗教自由正受到攻击。

sentences.en: Take the protracted campaign against the Little Sisters of the Poor.
sentences.zh: 以针对“贫苦小修女”的漫长诉讼为例。

sentences.en: He lists a bunch of cases in which he says religious people had been powerfully mistreated, notably
sentences.zh: 他列举了一系列案件，称宗教人士受到了严重的虐待，尤其是

sentences.en: the Little Sisters of the Poor, an order of Catholic nuns that didn't want to provide contraception coverage to its workers, but also...
sentences.zh: “贫苦小修女”，这是一个天主教修女会，她们不愿意为员工提供避孕药具报销，还有……

sentences.en: Jack Phillips, the owner of the now notorious Masterpiece Cake Shop.
sentences.zh: 杰克·菲利普斯，也就是如今臭名昭著的“杰作蛋糕店”的老板。

sentences.en: A cake baker in Colorado who refused to bake a cake for a same-sex couple.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州的一位蛋糕师，他拒绝为一对同性伴侣制作蛋糕。

sentences.en: A pharmacy called Ralph's was owned by a Christian family.
sentences.zh: 一家名为“拉尔夫”的药店，由一个基督教家庭拥有。

sentences.en: And a pharmacist who didn't want to fulfill some contraceptive prescriptions.
sentences.zh: 还有一名药剂师，他不想配发某些避孕药物处方。

sentences.en: A great many Americans disagree, sometimes quite strongly, with the religious beliefs of the Little Sisters, the owners of Ralph's, and Jack Phillips.
sentences.zh: 相当多的美国人并不同意小修女、“拉尔夫”药店老板以及杰克·菲利普斯的宗教信仰，有时甚至意见相当强烈。

sentences.en: And of course, they have a perfect right to do so.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们完全有权利这么做。

sentences.en: That is not the question.
sentences.zh: 问题不在这里。

sentences.en: The question we face is whether our society will be inclusive enough to tolerate people with unpopular religious beliefs.
sentences.zh: 我们面临的问题是，我们的社会是否足够包容，能够容忍那些持有不受欢迎的宗教信仰的人。

sentences.en: So all of these people, he says, have been marginalized.
sentences.zh: 因此，他说，所有这些人均已被边缘化。

sentences.en: They will risk being labeled as bigots and treated as such by governments, employers, and schools.
sentences.zh: 他们面临着被贴上偏执狂标签的风险，并受到政府、雇主和学校的如此对待。

sentences.en: Cast out of polite society merely for trying to follow their faith.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为试图遵循他们的信仰，就被主流社会抛弃。

sentences.en: Consider where things stood in the 1990s, when a Supreme Court decision called...
sentences.zh: 想想上世纪90年代的情况，当时最高法院的一项判决被称为……

sentences.en: And he suggests it's as a consequence of this 1990 decision, which requires people to knuckle under, he would say, to neutral laws of general applicability.
sentences.zh: 他暗示，这是1990年那项判决的结果，该判决用他的话说，要求人们屈服于普遍适用的中立法律。

sentences.en: For all Americans, standing up for our Constitution and our freedom is work that lies ahead.
sentences.zh: 对于所有美国人来说，捍卫我们的宪法和自由是我们接下来要做的工作。

sentences.en: And he goes on to say that the law should carve out space for religious people not to have to support and participate in things that violate their conscience.
sentences.zh: 他接着说道，法律应该为宗教人士留出空间，让他们不必支持和参与那些违背其良知的事情。

sentences.en: But when we meet next year, I hope we will be able to say that progress was made.
sentences.zh: 但当我们明年再聚时，我希望我们能说我们取得了进展。

sentences.en: Until then, I wish you all the beSt.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我祝愿大家一切都好。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: But of course, that raises a fundamental question about religion in a democracy, which is who
sentences.zh: 但当然，这引发了一个关于民主制度中宗教的根本问题，即在社会中，谁

sentences.en: should have to make accommodations in a society, the religious person or the secular society.
sentences.zh: 应该做出妥协，是宗教人士还是世俗社会。

sentences.en: And if I'm a gay couple that walks into that bakery not accommodating me, not making a cake
sentences.zh: 如果我是走进那家蛋糕店的一对同性伴侣，对方不肯迁就我、不为我的婚礼制作蛋糕，

sentences.en: for my wedding, that sure looks like bias and bigotry, and it looks like illegal discrimination.
sentences.zh: 那看起来确实像是偏见和狭隘，也像是违法的歧视。

sentences.en: But if I'm the religious owner of that bakery, forcing me to bake that cake may feel anti-religious.
sentences.zh: 但如果我是那家蛋糕店笃信宗教的老板，强迫我烤那个蛋糕可能会让我觉得是对宗教的冒犯。

sentences.en: It may feel like a legal impingement on my faith, government telling me to violate my deeply held beliefs.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让我觉得是对我信仰的法律侵犯，是政府在命令我违背自己深信不疑的信念。

sentences.en: So this becomes a very complicated question of who's supposed to make the sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就变成了一个非常复杂的问题，即究竟谁该做出牺牲。

sentences.en: Right, and these two sets of values may not be able to be accommodated.
sentences.zh: 没错，这两套价值观可能无法调和。

sentences.en: It may be that one has to win and one has to lose.
sentences.zh: 很可能必须有一方胜利，另一方失败。

sentences.en: And at the risk of repeating myself, the Constitution does protect the free exercise of religion.
sentences.zh: 冒着重复自己的风险，宪法确实保护宗教自由的行使。

sentences.en: And it means something.
sentences.zh: 这是有实际意义的。

sentences.en: Whether it means quite as much as what the majority on the Supreme Court now says, that's the battleground we're now fighting on.
sentences.zh: 至于它的意义是否如最高法院多数派现在所说的那样重大，这就是我们目前正在激烈争夺的战场。

sentences.en: Adam, from what you've said, almost all these religious liberty cases have stemmed from this sense
sentences.zh: 亚当，根据你所说，几乎所有这些宗教自由案件都源于这样一种感觉

sentences.en: that religious people are being trampled by secular law, and that the majority of Americans are essentially imposing a will on a minority of Americans.
sentences.zh: 即宗教人士正被世俗法律践踏，大多数美国人本质上是在把自己的意志强加给少数美国人。

sentences.en: That seems to be the dynamic.
sentences.zh: 这似乎就是这种动态。

sentences.en: But given the volume of victories at the Supreme Court that you have just described, it no longer
sentences.zh: 但鉴于你刚刚描述的最高法院一系列胜诉，这或许

sentences.en: perhaps feels like this is about a small group of people under attack seeking mere carve-outs and exemptions.
sentences.zh: 不再让人觉得这是一小群遭到攻击的人在寻求特例和豁免。

sentences.en: Is this now potentially a moment in American legal history where religious people, in the eyes of the law, are actually starting to be truly preferred by the law?
sentences.zh: 在法律眼中，这是否可能是美国法律史上的一个时刻，宗教人士实际上开始真正受到法律的优待？

sentences.en: And does that then undermine the argument that religion and religious people are under attack?
sentences.zh: 这难道不会削弱那种认为宗教和宗教人士正受到攻击的论点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's a curious part of the Alito speech where he says in some quarters, religious liberty is no longer a favored right.
sentences.zh: 是的，阿利托的演讲中有一个奇怪的部分，他说在某些圈子里，宗教自由不再是一项受青睐的权利。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure what quarters he's talking about, but I know what quarters he's not talking about, which is the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 我不确定他说的是哪些圈子，但我知道他没说的是哪些圈子，那就是最高法院。

sentences.en: In the Supreme Court, as you say, Michael, religious groups, and let's face it, particularly Christian religious groups, have achieved really a special status.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，迈克尔，在最高法院，宗教团体——坦白说，特别是基督教宗教团体——确实取得了特殊的地位。

sentences.en: So the notion that religious people are under attack is in real tension, at least at the court.
sentences.zh: 因此，“宗教人士正遭受攻击”这种观点存在真正的矛盾，至少在最高法院是如此。

sentences.en: Maybe in other aspects of society, Justice Alito is right.
sentences.zh: 也许在社会的其他方面，阿利托大法官是对的。

sentences.en: But at the court, the story is the opposite of the one he tells.
sentences.zh: 但在最高法院，情况与他所说的完全相反。

sentences.en: At the court, the story is of a triumphant series of huge victories for religion.
sentences.zh: 在最高法院，情况是宗教迎来了一系列辉煌的巨大胜利。

sentences.en: So Adam, given that, what is the next chapter in this legal debate at the Supreme Court over religious liberty?
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，鉴于此，最高法院关于宗教自由的这场法律辩论的下一章是什么？

sentences.en: Well, we have one big religion case this term.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在本期审理中有一个重大的宗教案件。

sentences.en: The case involves Philadelphia's foster care system.
sentences.zh: 这个案件涉及费城的寄养系统。

sentences.en: The city runs it.
sentences.zh: 该市负责运营这个系统。

sentences.en: It contracts with private groups to screen potential foster parents.
sentences.zh: 它与私人团体签约来筛选潜在的寄养父母。

sentences.en: Catholic charities have long participated in this program.
sentences.zh: 天主教慈善机构长期以来一直参与这个项目。

sentences.en: But the contract they have to sign with the city says you can't discriminate based on sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 但他们必须与该市签署的合同规定，你不能基于性取向进行歧视。

sentences.en: You have to allow same-sex couples to participate.
sentences.zh: 你必须允许同性伴侣参与。

sentences.en: And the Catholic charities say, no, thank you.
sentences.zh: 而天主教慈善机构说，不用了，谢谢。

sentences.en: We want to participate, but we'd like to rewrite the contract because we have a religious objection to same-sex couples serving as foster parents.
sentences.zh: 我们想参与，但我们想重写合同，因为我们对同性伴侣担任寄养父母有宗教方面的异议。

sentences.en: And at the argument, the court went down this same road we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 在法庭辩论中，法院走上了我们一直在讨论的同一条道路。

sentences.en: Are there exceptions that apply in other settings?
sentences.zh: 是否存在适用于其他环境的例外情况？

sentences.en: Does the city sometimes take account of, say, race in whom it's going to place children with in the best interests of the child?
sentences.zh: 为了儿童的最大利益，该市在安置儿童时是否有时会考虑种族等因素？

sentences.en: And the suggestion from some of the conservative justices was, well, once you have some exception, you have to give an exception to the Catholic charity also.
sentences.zh: 一些保守派大法官的暗示是，好吧，一旦你有了某种例外，你也必须给天主教慈善机构一个例外。

sentences.en: So you have this same dynamic we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以你们看到了我们一直在讨论的这种相同的动态。

sentences.en: And if they rule, as I expect they will, for the Catholic charities, the court could do one of two things.
sentences.zh: 如果他们像我预期的那样裁决天主教慈善机构胜诉，法院可以做两件事之一。

sentences.en: It could overrule the 1990 case entirely.
sentences.zh: 它可以完全推翻1990年的那个案件。

sentences.en: It's been asked to do that.
sentences.zh: 有人要求它这么做。

sentences.en: That's part of the case.
sentences.zh: 这是案件的一部分。

sentences.en: That could happen.
sentences.zh: 这可能会发生。

sentences.en: Or it could say, as soon as anybody gets an exception, the Catholic charities have to get an exception too.
sentences.zh: 或者它可以说，一旦任何人获得了例外，天主教慈善机构也必须获得例外。

sentences.en: And because of the way the foster care program is set up, somebody somewhere is going to get an exception to something.
sentences.zh: 由于寄养程序设置的方式，总会有某人在某处获得某事的例外。

sentences.en: And therefore, the 1990 decision remains in place in name.
sentences.zh: 因此，1990年的裁决名义上依然存在。

sentences.en: But it's been recharacterized, recast, and hollowed out to such an extent that it almost doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 但它已经被重新定义、重新塑造并被掏空到这种程度，以至于它几乎变得无关紧要了。

sentences.en: And either way, under either rationale, what we end up with is that religion and religious
sentences.zh: 无论如何，无论基于哪种法理依据，我们最终看到的结果是，宗教和宗教团体

sentences.en: groups under this Supreme Court will have achieved a very special status in American society and law.
sentences.zh: 在该最高法院的主导下，将在美国社会和法律中获得一种非常特殊的地位。

sentences.en: Thank you, Adam.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，亚当。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: This morning, the FDA and CDC announced that out of an abundance of caution, we're recommending a pause in the use of the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine.
sentences.zh: 今天上午，美国食品药品监督管理局和疾病控制与预防中心宣布，出于谨慎考虑，我们建议暂停使用强生新冠疫苗。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, two key U.S.
sentences.zh: 周二，美国两个主要的

sentences.en: health agencies called for a temporary suspension of COVID-19 vaccinations using Johnson & Johnson's single-shot dose.
sentences.zh: 卫生机构呼吁暂停接种使用强生单剂疫苗的新冠疫苗接种工作。

sentences.en: After receiving reports of six cases in which recipients of the vaccine developed severe blood clots.
sentences.zh: 此前有报道称，接种该疫苗的接种者中出现了6起严重血栓病例。

sentences.en: Right now, I'd like to stress, these events appear to be extremely rare.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想强调的是，这些事件似乎极其罕见。

sentences.en: However, COVID-19 vaccine safety is a top priority for the federal government.
sentences.zh: 然而，新冠疫苗的安全性是联邦政府的重中之重。

sentences.en: And we take all reports of adverse events following vaccination very seriously.
sentences.zh: 我们非常严肃地对待所有关于疫苗接种后不良事件的报告。

sentences.en: The six cases, out of nearly 7 million doses administered, all occurred in women within about two weeks of vaccination.
sentences.zh: 在接种的近700万剂疫苗中，这6起病例全部发生在女性身上，且都在接种后两周左右出现。

sentences.en: After the announcement, many states immediately followed the federal guidance and said they
sentences.zh: 公告发布后，许多州立即效仿联邦指导方针，表示将

sentences.en: would pause injection of Johnson & Johnson's vaccine, one of three COVID vaccines authorized for emergency use in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 暂停注射强生疫苗，这是美国授权紧急使用的三种新冠疫苗之一。

sentences.en: And President Biden has decided to withdraw all American troops from Afghanistan by September
sentences.zh: 拜登总统已决定在9月

sentences.en: 11th, 20 years after terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon prompted the U.S.

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
